title: Sync engine orchestration (background, offline, conflict policy)

tasks.title: Add SyncError variants and the sync module scaffold
acceptance: `src/error.rs` gains `SyncError` (thiserror, `#[non_exhaustive]`) with at least the variants `Api { source: ApiError }`, `Store { message: String }`, `Queue { message: String }`, `Offline`, `ChannelClosed` and `Cancelled`
`AppError` gains `Sync(#[from] SyncError)` and renders it with a `sync: ` prefix, matching the existing `Config(..)`/`Auth(..)`/`Api(..)` style
`SyncError::is_offline(&self) -> bool` returns true for `Offline` and for `Api { source }` where the underlying `ApiError` is a transport error; unit-tested per variant
A unit test formats every `SyncError` variant with `{}` and `{:?}` and asserts the fixture token `tok_fake_abc123` never appears
`src/sync/mod.rs` exists with module docs and the same module-scope `#![allow(dead_code)]` pattern used by `src/api/mod.rs`; `src/main.rs` declares `mod sync;`
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Mirrors T-201 (EPIC-03) which introduced `ApiError` and `src/api/mod.rs`. Error-type-and-wiring only, no engine logic, so the rest of the epic can land in parallel. Reuse the crate-wide `Result<T> = Result<T, AppError>` alias and never interpolate token material (see the `Secret` helper in `src/log.rs`, which must not be modified).

tasks.title: SyncState event enum and state transition rules
acceptance: `SyncState` enum exists with exactly the variants `Syncing`, `Synced { at: OffsetDateTime }` (or the crate's existing timestamp type), `Offline`, `Pending { count: usize }` and `Error { msg: String }`; it derives `Debug`, `Clone`, `PartialEq`
`Error { msg }` is constructed via a helper `SyncState::from_error(&SyncError)` that uses the `Display` text, so no secret material can reach the UI (unit test asserts a token fixture never appears)

A `SyncStatus` holder keeps the latest state plus the pending-command count and exposes `apply(SyncState) -> bool` returning false when the new state is identical to the current one (duplicate-event suppression), unit-tested
`Pending { count: 0 }` applied while the current state is `Synced{..}` does not overwrite it (unit test): pending count 0 is reported through the holder, not as a state
`src/sync/mod.rs` declares `mod state;` and re-exports `SyncState`
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Pure types + transition logic, no tokio and no IO, so it can be unit-tested without fakes. EPIC-07 renders these events; keep the enum small and serialisation-free. Timestamp type: use whatever date/time type the EPIC-03 model layer already pulls in (`src/api/model/common.rs`) rather than adding a new dependency.

tasks.title: Engine ports: Cache, WriteQueue and SyncApi traits with test fakes
acceptance: `src/sync/ports.rs` defines three async traits the engine depends on: `SyncApi` (`async fn sync(&self, req: &SyncRequest) -> Result<SyncResponse>`), `Cache` (`sync_token()`, `set_sync_token()`, `apply_response()`, `full_sync_date_utc()`) and `WriteQueue` (`pending_batch()`, `pending_count()`, `apply_sync_status()`, `resolve_temp_ids()`)
All three traits are `Send + Sync` and object-safe behind `async_trait` (or equivalent), so the engine can be generic over them
`SyncClient` from `src/api/client.rs` implements `SyncApi` with a thin forwarding impl and no behaviour change

`src/sync/fakes.rs` is `#[cfg(test)]`-or-`#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-fakes"))]` gated and provides in-memory `FakeCache`, `FakeQueue` and `FakeApi` that record every call and allow scripting responses/errors per call
A unit test drives `FakeApi` through one success and one transport error and asserts the recorded call log
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: This task is the seam that decouples EPIC-06 from the in-flight EPIC-04 cache and EPIC-05 write queue: the engine talks only to these traits, and the real adapters are wired in T-510 once those epics land. Model the trait method shapes on `SyncRequest`/`SyncResponse` in `src/api/sync.rs` (`sync_token`, `full_sync`, `temp_id_mapping`, `sync_status`, `full_sync_date_utc`). Do not implement storage or queue semantics here.

tasks.title: SyncHandle: trigger and event channels with trigger collapsing
acceptance: `SyncHandle` exposes `trigger()` (non-blocking, never awaits network) and `subscribe() -> Receiver<SyncState>`; it is `Clone` and `Send + Sync`
Triggers use a capacity-1 / coalescing channel: N triggers sent while a cycle is running collapse into at most one queued follow-up run (unit test sends 10 triggers and asserts exactly 1 pending)
`trigger()` on a shut-down engine returns `Err(SyncError::ChannelClosed)` instead of panicking (unit test)
Event sending is lossy-tolerant: a slow or dropped subscriber never blocks or fails the engine (unit test drops the receiver then triggers an event and asserts no error)
`shutdown()` signals the engine loop to stop and is idempotent (unit test calls it twice)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Channels only, no cycle logic - the UI side of the contract (EPIC-07 holds a `SyncHandle`). Use `tokio::sync` primitives already available via the `tokio` dependency in `Cargo.toml` (enable only the `sync` feature if it is missing; do not touch `Cargo.lock` pins beyond that).

tasks.title: Sync cycle: full-vs-incremental token selection and delta apply
acceptance: `SyncCycle::run_once()` reads the token from the `Cache` port: `None` → request built with `SyncRequest::full()` (`sync_token: "*"`), `Some(t)` → `SyncRequest::incremental(t)`
With a fake cache holding no token, exactly one API call is made and its body carries `sync_token: "*"` (asserted against the recorded request)
After a successful response the new `sync_token` is persisted through the `Cache` port before the cycle returns; a second `run_once()` uses that token
A response with `full_sync: true` is applied with replace semantics and `full_sync: false` with delta semantics, passed through to `Cache::apply_response` with the flag intact (asserted on the fake)
An API error leaves the stored `sync_token` unchanged (unit test: token after failed cycle == token before)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Pull half of the cycle only; the flush half lands in T-506. Reuse the existing constructors `SyncRequest::full()` / `SyncRequest::incremental()` in `src/api/sync.rs` rather than hand-building request bodies, and let the EPIC-03 retry policy in `src/api/retry.rs` handle in-request retries - the engine must not add its own per-request retry loop.

tasks.title: Flush-then-pull ordering and command result handling in one cycle
acceptance: `run_once()` performs flush-then-pull in a single `/sync` request per cycle: pending commands from `WriteQueue::pending_batch()` are attached to the same request that carries the sync token (asserted on the recorded request)
Command order from the queue is preserved in the request `commands` array (unit test with 3 commands asserts order)

`temp_id_mapping` from the response is handed to `WriteQueue::resolve_temp_ids()` before `sync_status` is applied, and both run before the response resources are applied to the cache (call-order assertion on the fakes)
`sync_status` outcomes are forwarded verbatim to `WriteQueue::apply_sync_status()`; the engine itself never decides ok-vs-failed semantics (that is EPIC-05)
An empty queue produces a pull-only request with no `commands` key (unit test)
A failed flush (API error) does not advance the sync token and does not mark any command as delivered (unit test)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Depends on the EPIC-05 write queue existing behind the `WriteQueue` port from T-503 - do not reach into EPIC-05 internals or re-implement idempotency/uuid handling here; the engine only sequences the calls. Scope note: this task is pure orchestration inside `cycle.rs`, no new modules.

tasks.title: Conflict policy FR-18: server wins, pending local commands replayed (LWW)
acceptance: After the server response is applied to the cache, any command still `pending` in the queue is re-applied optimistically on top, so the local value wins for fields the user changed while offline/in-flight
Unit test: item X has remote content `"remote"` in the pulled response and a pending local `item_update` setting `"local"` → cache ends the cycle with `"local"`
Unit test: item X changed remotely only (no pending command touching X) → cache ends the cycle with the remote value
Commands that were acknowledged `ok` in this cycle's `sync_status` are not replayed (unit test asserts no double-apply)
Replay is scoped to the resources present in the response - a pending command for an untouched resource triggers no cache write (unit test asserts the fake cache call count)
The policy is documented in module docs with an explicit `FR-18` reference
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Replay uses the EPIC-05 optimistic-apply path through the `WriteQueue`/`Cache` ports; EPIC-06 owns the *policy* (when to replay), EPIC-05 owns the per-command semantics. Keep the decision logic in `conflict.rs` and call it from the end of `cycle.rs::run_once`.

tasks.title: Full-sync lag detection with immediate incremental follow-up
acceptance: A helper parses `full_sync_date_utc` from the response and compares it to the current clock through an injected clock trait (no `SystemTime::now()` inside the logic)

`full_sync: true` with `full_sync_date_utc` older than the lag threshold (constant, documented, default 5 minutes) → the cycle immediately runs one extra incremental sync with the freshly stored token (unit test asserts exactly 2 API calls, second one incremental)
`full_sync_date_utc` within the threshold → exactly 1 API call (unit test)
Missing or unparseable `full_sync_date_utc` is treated as no lag and logged at debug level, never an error (unit test)
The follow-up incremental never recurses: at most one extra sync per cycle, even if the follow-up response also reports lag (unit test)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: `SyncResponse::full_sync_date_utc` is already an `Option<String>` in `src/api/sync.rs`. Follow the injected-clock pattern established by `Sleeper`/`RecordingSleeper` in `src/api/retry.rs` so tests never sleep for real.

tasks.title: Offline detection and bounded retry backoff
acceptance: A transport-class `SyncError` (see `SyncError::is_offline`) moves the engine to `SyncState::Offline`; non-transport errors emit `SyncState::Error { msg }` and keep the engine online
While offline, retry intervals grow exponentially from the configured `sync_interval` up to a documented cap (default 5 minutes) - asserted via the injected clock, no real sleeping
Attempt rate is bounded: a unit test simulating 30 minutes of downtime asserts the number of API attempts is ≤ the documented maximum (no retry storm)
The first success after an outage resets the backoff to `sync_interval` and emits `SyncState::Synced { at }` (unit test)
A manual trigger while offline attempts a sync immediately (bypasses the current backoff) at most once per trigger (unit test)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Backoff math should reuse or mirror `RetryPolicy` in `src/api/retry.rs` (exponential + jitter, injected `Sleeper`) rather than inventing a second scheme; this layer is about *between-cycle* pacing, while `RetryPolicy` covers *within-request* retries. Cache edits must keep working while offline - this module must never gate local writes.

tasks.title: Sync actor: tokio task wiring scheduler, triggers and run de-duplication
acceptance: `SyncEngine::spawn(api, cache, queue, config) -> SyncHandle` starts one `tokio` task that owns the API client, cache and queue; the handle is the only way to interact with it
The loop selects over the `sync_interval` tick, the trigger channel and the shutdown signal; `sync_interval` is read from `Config` in `src/config/model.rs` (no new config key)
Overlapping runs are de-duplicated: triggers arriving during an in-flight cycle cause exactly one follow-up cycle (unit test with a slow fake API asserts cycle count)
Each cycle emits `Syncing` at start and then exactly one terminal state (`Synced`/`Offline`/`Error`), plus a `Pending{n}` update whenever the pending count changes (unit test on the event stream)
`shutdown()` ends the task within one cycle and an in-flight cycle is allowed to finish or is cancelled cleanly without poisoning the cache (unit test asserts the task joins)
The engine never blocks the caller: `trigger()` returns before any network call (unit test with a fake API that never resolves)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: This is the assembly task: it only wires T-505..T-509 together. `tokio` currently enables `rt-multi-thread` and `macros` in `Cargo.toml`; add `sync`/`time` features if missing but do not change pinned versions or `rust-toolchain.toml`. Keep the actor generic over the T-503 ports so tests use the fakes and real adapters (EPIC-04 cache, EPIC-05 queue) are injected at the call site.

tasks.title: Integration test: scheduled and on-demand sync against a mock API
acceptance: Test harness spins up the engine with a mocked HTTP sync endpoint (same mock-server approach used by the EPIC-03 API integration tests) and a short `sync_interval`
First run with an empty cache issues exactly one request whose body has `sync_token: "*"`; the second run uses the token returned by the mock (both asserted on the recorded requests)
A remote-only change served by the mock appears in the cache within one `sync_interval`, and immediately when `trigger()` is called
A local pending command is flushed and its effect is visible in the following pull within a single cycle; wall-clock latency of that round trip is asserted < 5s
Overlapping triggers during a slow mock response result in exactly one extra cycle, asserted via the mock's request count
`cargo test --all` passes with no `#[ignore]` and no reliance on real network or real `sync_interval` waits > 2s
tasks.context: Use fixture JSON bodies rather than live API captures; no real tokens or account data (fake token `tok_fake_abc123`). Depends on the EPIC-04 cache and EPIC-05 write queue existing - if the real adapters are not merged yet, drive the test through the T-503 ports with in-memory implementations and leave a TODO noting the swap.

tasks.title: Integration test: offline resilience and LWW conflict resolution
acceptance: Mock API refusing connections → engine emits `SyncState::Offline`, local edits still apply to the cache, and the attempt count over a simulated outage stays within the documented cap (no retry storm)
When the mock comes back, all queued commands flush with each client `uuid` seen exactly once across the whole test (zero duplicates, zero losses)

Conflict scenario: item edited remotely in the mock response and also pending locally → after one cycle the final cached value is the local one, and the remote value was applied first (assert ordering via cache history or the applied-value sequence)
A non-transport failure (mock returns 401) produces `SyncState::Error { msg }`, not `Offline`, and does not wipe the cache
Emitted `SyncState` sequence over the whole scenario is asserted explicitly and contains no state carrying token material
`cargo test --all` passes with no `#[ignore]`
tasks.context: Shares the fixture helpers with T-511; coordinate so `tests/support/sync_fixtures.rs` is written once (T-511 creates it, this task extends it) to avoid a merge conflict. Fake token only - never a real Todoist token in fixtures.

tasks.title: Document the sync engine: lifecycle, states, conflict policy and tuning
acceptance: `docs/sync-engine.md` describes the cycle (flush → pull → temp-id resolution → conflict replay), the `SyncState` events and what each means to the user
The FR-18 conflict policy (server state wins, pending local commands replayed on top = LWW) is stated with the worked example from T-507
Offline behaviour and the backoff cap are documented, including the maximum attempt rate asserted in T-512
Tuning section explains `sync_interval` (default 60s) and the full-sync lag threshold, linking to `src/config/model.rs`
README gains a short 'Sync behaviour' section linking to `docs/sync-engine.md`
No secrets, real account ids or live API captures appear in the docs
tasks.context: Documentation only - no code changes. Match the tone and structure of the existing docs in `docs/`. Numbers quoted (thresholds, caps, defaults) must match the constants actually shipped in T-508/T-509, not the plan.
